1 مَأَدَ , aor.
مَاَ^َ , (S, L, K,) inf. n. مَأْدٌ, (S, L,) It (a plant, L, K, and a tree, L, and a branch, S, L) was, or became, flourishing and fresh, and soft, tender, and supple: (L:) or it quivered, shook, or played loosely, and was, or became, succulent, or sappy, (L, K,) and flourishing and fresh, and soft, tender, and supple: (K:) it (a branch or twig) became filled with its first sap: and مَؤُدَ, aor.
مَاُ^َ , it (a plant) became succulent, or sappy. (L.) يَمْأَدُ مَأْدًا حَسَنًا It (a branch) is [beautifully] soft, tender, and supple, and quivering. (S, L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
